subject: chemistry
title: Acids & Bases Adventure 2: Ka, Kb and weak acid pH
welcome_lead: Today you'll find pH of weak acids using Ka and pKa.
meta_desc: Chemistry HL — Ka, pKa, weak acid pH, Kb, conjugate strength.
final_note: You learned Ka = [H⁺][A⁻]/[HA]; pKa = -log Ka; lower pKa = stronger acid; for weak acid, [H⁺] ≈ √(Ka·c).

walkthroughs.body_html:
For HA ⇌ H⁺ + A⁻:

Ka = [H⁺][A⁻] / [HA]

Lower Ka → less dissociation → weaker acid. pKa = -log Ka.

- HCl: pKa ≈ -7 (very strong).
- HF: pKa = 3.2.
- CH₃COOH: pKa = 4.76.
- HCN: pKa = 9.3.

For weak acid of conc. c with Ka:

Assume [H⁺] = [A⁻] = x, [HA] ≈ c (small dissociation).

Ka ≈ x² / c → x = √(Ka · c)

Example: 0.10 mol/dm³ CH₃COOH, Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵.
[H⁺] = √(1.8 × 10⁻⁵ × 0.10) = 1.34 × 10⁻³.
pH = 2.87.

Stronger acid → weaker conjugate base, and vice versa.

Ka × Kb = Kw

so pKa + pKb = 14 at 298 K.

HCl strong (low pKa) → Cl⁻ very weak base (won't pull H⁺ from water).
